diagnosis.what_happened: academic-writer generated a gold standard chapter 4 with OpenXML sequence violations, justification stripping due to brittle string heuristics, and untranslated English statistical terms.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: This led to corrupted Word documents, improperly formatted table captions, and violation of Persian academic language standards.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: The agent should have adhered to CT_TblPr schema ordering, used structural checks instead of string-matching for justification, and translated all statistical abbreviations to Persian.
diagnosis.rationale_why: OpenXML relies on strict schema sequencing. Brittle text-matching heuristics fail on narrative text containing keywords. Persian academic texts require complete localization of terms.

desired_behavior: Strictly insert <w:bidiVisual/> before <w:tblW> in OpenXML. Use structural heuristics for justification instead of naive string matching. Always translate English statistical abbreviations to Persian in data tuples.
generalization: Robust document generation requires strict schema adherence, structural (not string-based) heuristics, and comprehensive localization protocols.

evidence.observed_value: Validation failure with OpenXML schema violation, brittle justification stripping, and untranslated lexicon
evidence.threshold_value: Zero OpenXML schema errors, robust formatting, and fully translated tables
